re_line: Lee reshuffles security team, names first female spy chief · KOSPI drops 3.3%, government prepares market stabilization fund · Kim holds first-ever direct ambassador credentials ceremony
morning_memo: President Lee Jae-myung replaced his foreign minister, spy chief, and unification minister, naming the first woman to head the National Intelligence Service.
KOSPI fell 3.3% to 4,708 as AI-sector selloff spread; the government activated market stabilization preparations, including easing share buyback limits for three months.
Kim Jong Un personally received credentials from 10 ambassadors for the first time in over 30 years, declaring North Korea seeks no hegemony or expansion.

on_this_day.event: North Korea fired approximately 170 artillery rounds at Yeonpyeong Island, killing two ROK Marines and two civilians in the first artillery attack on South Korean territory since the Korean War.
on_this_day.relevance: The shelling remains the benchmark event for West Sea NLL escalation; ROK Marine Corps Commandant Gen. Ju Il-suk noted as recently as October 2026 that North Korea has made various changes to forces facing South Korea's border islands.

key_stat.label: Value of Vietnam high-speed rail design contract won by Korean consortium
key_stat.context: A consortium including Korea National Railway Corp., Sambo Engineering, and Yooshin Engineering, alongside France's Systra and Vietnam's Tedi, won the 560-billion-won feasibility study and preliminary basic design contract for Vietnam's North-South high-speed railway, the largest overseas rail planning and design deal Korea has secured abroad.

bp_locations.name: Yongbyon Nuclear Complex
bp_locations.note: As of April 2026: Enrichment building expansion complete, new centrifuge hall operational. 5 MWe reactor and IRT-2000 both running. Thermal signatures consistent with increased plutonium/HEU production.

bp_locations.name: Sinpo South Shipyard
bp_locations.note: As of May 2025: Hero Kim Kun Ok SLBM submarine exited drydock after more than two years of fitting-out but was still not operational. New submarine construction begun in separate bay. NK Pro satellite analysis (Oct 20 2026) separately reports North Korea's Nampho Shipyard missed a deadline earlier in Oct 2026 to launch a 5,000-ton naval destroyer, with hull sections visible at two potential outdoor assembly areas. 38 North analysis published Oct 30 documents public display of a vessel described as a 'Tactical Nuclear Attack' submarine. Kim Jong Un inspected Nampho Shipyard on Nov 7 (reported Nov 8 by KCNA), announcing a new warship under construction larger than the destroyer built last year. NK News reported on Nov 6 that North Korea has expanded warship construction to a third shipyard. 38 North published analysis on Nov 11 of the Choe Hyon destroyer and its strategic implications for the West Sea Fleet. NK News identified a second major east-coast naval base project on Nov 13, beyond the Munchon-area site Kim inspected on Nov 12.

bp_locations.name: THAAD Site, Seongju County
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: All 6 THAAD launchers were redeployed to the Middle East amid Iran tensions. At least 2 launchers may have returned to Seongju by late March 2026. Battery operational status remains uncertain. This report is from March 2026 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Sohae Satellite Launch Station
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: 2,500 kN engine test stand firing observed. Two villages razed for facility expansion. New seaport and large assembly building nearing completion. This report is from March 2026 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Punggye-ri Nuclear Test Site
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: ROK Defense Intelligence Agency assessed Tunnel No. 3 is test-ready and a nuclear test can be conducted at any time upon political decision. Site maintained at high readiness since mid-2024. This report is from November 2025 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Tumangang–Khasan (NK-Russia border)
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: Road bridge construction accelerated, completion target moved to Summer 2026. Passenger rail service resumed mid-2025. Ore and tank car traffic at highest levels since project began. Russian Transport Ministry applications filed November 13, 2026 for a 14-daily-round-trip Vladivostok-Rason bus route over the new vehicle bridge, with experts noting the service will likely transport DPRK workers more than Russian tourists.

bp_locations.name: Sinuiju–Dandong (NK-China border)
bp_locations.note: NK News Planet Labs satellite imagery analyzed through November 15, 2026 confirms trucks filling Sinuiju customs facility from October 16, the day after the New Yalu River Bridge officially opened, with activity peaking October 19–20. A wall of 40-foot containers bearing Maersk and COSCO markings was visible on the Chinese side. Kim Jong Un crossed the New Yalu River Bridge on October 24 during his unannounced visit to Dandong. Daily NK reported November 18 that Sinuiju markets are overflowing with Chinese goods but a severe cash shortage means almost nobody is buying, with vendors describing a 'trading cliff.' Daily NK reported November 23 that low-income families in Sinuiju are sinking into crisis as market prices for food and daily necessities soar despite state promotion of Sinuiju development as a model for regional growth.

bp_locations.name: Rason SEZ
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: Chinese businesspeople re-entry to Rason SEZ expanded. Coal exports through Rason at highest levels in years throughout 2025. Arms export berth also active. This report is from November 2025 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea NLL
bp_locations.note: Herald Economy reported November 23 that a North Korean vessel marked 'Marine Police' was spotted near Yeonpyeong Island, with the ROK Joint Chiefs confirming they are tracking and monitoring the vessel. As of September 26, 2025: 140m DPRK merchant vessel Toksong crossed the Northern Limit Line near Baengnyeong Island, advanced 5km south. ROK Marine Corps Commandant Gen. Ju Il-suk stated October 20, 2026 that North Korea has made 'various changes' to forces facing South Korea's border islands.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea PMZ
bp_locations.note: As of January 27-28, 2026: Atlantic Amsterdam (converted oil rig, Chinese aquaculture platform) relocated out of the Provisional Measures Zone to Weihai shipyard following President Lee Jae-myung's Beijing state visit. Two giant aquaculture cages (Shen Lan 1, Shen Lan 2) and 13 buoys remain in the PMZ. This report is from January 2026 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Vostochny/Dunai
bp_locations.note: As of January 2026: Arms shipments slowed due to ice, one Russian vessel (likely Angara or Lady R) visited Rason, docked January 14, 2026 at arms export berth. Cargo routed to Vostochny. Since September 2023: 64 voyages by 4 vessels (Angara, Maria, Maya-1, Lady R) delivered approximately 15,800 containers (approximately 4.2-5.8 million munitions) from Rajin to Vostochny/Dunai. Russian Transport Ministry applications filed November 13, 2026 for a Vladivostok-Rason bus route operating 14 daily round trips.

top_stories.headline: Lee reshuffles security team, names first female spy chief in NIS history
top_stories.body: President **Lee Jae-myung** nominated former Justice Minister **Kang Kum-sil** as National Intelligence Service director, a move that, if confirmed, would make her the first woman to head South Korea's spy agency since its 1961 founding. Second Deputy National Security Adviser **Lim Woong-soon**, a career diplomat with extensive experience in US affairs and former ambassador to Canada, was tapped as foreign minister, while former floor leader **Hong Ihk-pyo** was nominated as unification minister. Hankyoreh reported that a Blue House official characterized the reshuffle as aimed at redefining the NIS's legal and institutional role rather than expanding its inter-Korean function, with outgoing officials labeled as the 'self-reliance faction' and their replacements aligned more closely with the alliance-first camp.

top_stories.headline: Seoul activates market stabilization measures as KOSPI drops 3.3% on AI selloff fears
top_stories.body: Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance and Economy **Lee Hyoung Il** convened an emergency market review on November 22 and announced phased stabilization measures, including preparations to activate the Stock Market Stabilization Fund and a three-month easing of daily share-repurchase order limits for listed companies effective November 24. The Financial Services Commission formally approved the buyback rule change at its 20th regular meeting on November 23. The government characterized the selloff as driven by uncertainty over AI and semiconductor industry profitability, US data-center regulations, tighter semiconductor export controls, and potential US interest rate increases.

top_stories.headline: Kim Jong Un holds first direct ambassador credentials ceremony in over 30 years, cites East Asia security threat
top_stories.body: **Kim Jong Un** personally received credentials from ambassadors of 10 countries, Russia, Sweden, Indonesia, Vietnam, Brazil, the Czech Republic, India, the Philippines, Thailand, and Bangladesh, at the Workers' Party of Korea Central Committee headquarters on November 22, the first such direct reception in over 30 years according to Korea Times and financial news reports. Kim delivered a speech declaring that North Korea pursues no hegemony or expansion, framing the country's military buildup as the exercise of its sovereign right, and said the security situation in the DPRK and the East Asian political and military environment demand that Pyongyang provide for itself the power and capability to defend itself. KCNA reported Foreign Minister **Choe Son Hui** also attended.

also_today.headline: Russia proposes trilateral Tumen River survey with North Korea and China, tied to Beijing's Sea of Japan access ambitions
also_today.body_text: A Russian government order signed by Prime Minister **Mikhail Mishustin** on September 26 proposes that the Chinese and DPRK embassies in Moscow review a plan for a joint ecological survey of the Tumen River, mapping its depth, width, and underwater terrain, information relevant to assessing navigability. NK News notes the plan appears tied to Beijing's ambitions to gain access to the Sea of Japan through the Tumen corridor.

also_today.headline: WSJ: New satellite photos show expansion of North Korean uranium-enrichment plant
also_today.body_text: WSJ satellite photographs document expansion of the uranium-enrichment facility at Yongbyon, adding visual corroboration to assessments of an operational new centrifuge hall first reported in April 2026. The imagery was published as Kim Jong Un continued to deflect US summit overtures.

also_today.headline: North Korea shifts 2027 Pyongyang International Marathon from April to October
also_today.body_text: DPRK-focused travel agency Koryo Tours, the race's international partner, announced the 2027 Pyongyang International Marathon has been moved from its traditional April timing to October, adding to a pattern of uncertainty around North Korea's revival of international tourism.

us_korea_deals.state_of_play: Steel and aluminum remain at 50% and automobiles at 15%, both under Section 232. The Section 122 surcharge expired July 24, 2026, leaving no baseline reciprocal tariff rate in force. Section 301 investigations launched March 11, 2026 against 16 partners including South Korea are now the primary prospective tariff vehicle.

business_economy.headline: South Korea's early November exports gain after $1 trillion annual milestone
business_economy.body_text: South Korea's early export data for November showed gains following the country's annual export total crossing the $1 trillion milestone.

business_economy.headline: Korea Aerospace Industries announces 1.5 trillion won investment in Yeongnam-region aerospace and defense
business_economy.body_text: Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI) announced a *1.5 trillion won* investment in aerospace and defense sectors in the Yeongnam region, intended as a catalyst for advanced industry development in South Gyeongsang Province.

business_economy.headline: Korean-led consortium wins 560B-won Vietnam high-speed rail design contract, largest overseas rail deal in Korean history
business_economy.body_text: The ministry cited sustained summit diplomacy and a presidential letter as factors in winning competition against more than 40 global rail design firms.

business_economy.headline: Qatar calls South Korea 'essential' partner, seeks cooperation in AI, defense, and renewables beyond energy
business_economy.body_text: Qatar's Minister of State for Foreign Affairs **Sultan bin Saad Al Muraikhi** described Korea as an essential partner in Qatar's post-oil diversification during a bilateral policy meeting in Doha with Seoul's Deputy Minister for Political Affairs **Chung Eui-hae**, calling for expanded cooperation in artificial intelligence, the defense industry, renewable energy, and healthcare.

northeast_asia.headline: FM Cho Hyun meets Mongolian FM Battsetseg in Seoul, discusses Korean Peninsula peace and critical minerals
northeast_asia.body_text: Foreign Minister **Cho Hyun** met Mongolian Foreign Minister **Batmunkh Battsetseg** in Seoul, the first official visit by a Mongolian foreign minister in 10 years since September 2016, and discussed accelerating a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, expanding rare-mineral supply-chain cooperation through a joint rare metals center opening December 2025, and Mongolia's role in facilitating Korean Peninsula peace given Ulaanbaatar's friendly ties with both Koreas.

northeast_asia.headline: Deputy PM Lee: 'late-3% GDP growth possible this year; 2027 policy to focus on shared growth'
northeast_asia.body_text: Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister **Lee Hyoung Il** stated that growth in the high 3% range is achievable in 2026 and said 2027 economic policy will focus on 'growth for all,' with the government considering expanding small and medium enterprise participation in national projects to narrow industrial disparities.

gallup_spotlight.topic: College entrance exam integrity / AI cheating
gallup_spotlight.finding: A Gallup Korea poll released November 22 found 47% of respondents cited the economy as the most important issue heading into the next general election, with the Democratic Party holding a lead in party support.

rok_personnel.name: Kang Kum-sil
rok_personnel.detail: Former Justice Minister and former Global Climate and Environmental Affairs Ambassador Kang Kum-sil was nominated by President Lee Jae-myung; if confirmed after National Assembly hearing, she would become the first woman to head the NIS since its 1961 founding. Presidential chief of staff Lim Kwang-hyun cited her legal affairs background and international cooperation experience as qualifications for strengthening democratic oversight and addressing cyberthreats.

rok_personnel.name: Lim Woong-soon
rok_personnel.detail: Second Deputy National Security Adviser Lim Woong-soon, a career diplomat with extensive US-affairs experience and former ambassador to Canada, was nominated as foreign minister to replace Cho Hyun. Newsis reported that the appointment, alongside National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac's retention, is interpreted as a shift toward prioritizing the US alliance.

rok_government.official: Presidential Chief of Staff Lim Kwang-hyun
rok_government.action: President Lee announces five-post cabinet reshuffle including NIS chief, FM, and unification minister
rok_government.detail: Chief of Staff Lim Kwang-hyun announced the reshuffle at a press briefing, naming Kang Kum-sil as NIS director nominee, Lim Woong-soon as foreign minister nominee, Hong Ihk-pyo as unification minister nominee, Han Jun-ho as interior minister nominee, and Kang Yu-jung as culture minister nominee.

rok_government.action: Second Korea-Qatar Policy Consultations held in Doha; Qatar calls Korea 'essential' post-oil partner
rok_government.detail: Deputy Minister for Political Affairs Chung Eui-hae met Qatar's Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Sultan bin Saad Al Muraikhi in Doha on November 22 for the second Korea-Qatar Policy Consultations (first held November 2021), agreeing to expand cooperation from energy and infrastructure into AI, defense, renewables, and healthcare.

rok_government.action: MOFA and Overseas Construction Association update 19-year-old cooperation agreement to support Korean firms abroad
rok_government.detail: FM Cho Hyun and Korea Overseas Construction Association Chair Han Man-hee revised the 2007 inter-agency cooperation agreement, strengthening coordination to help Korean companies win and operate overseas construction projects amid geopolitical and economic security risks, using embassy networks to support firms.

rok_government.action: Korea and Australia hold 4th ASEAN Policy Dialogue in Canberra
rok_government.detail: Korea's ASEAN Bureau Director Kwon Jae-hwan and Australia's Southeast Asia Strategy and Development Director Justin Whyatt co-chaired the fourth Korea-Australia ASEAN Policy Dialogue in Canberra, sharing assessments of the regional security environment and discussing cooperation on maritime security, AI-digital transition, and Mekong sub-regional development.

rok_government.action: FSC eases daily treasury stock buyback limit for listed companies for three months effective Nov 24
rok_government.detail: The FSC at its 20th regular meeting on November 23 voted to ease the daily buying-order limit on treasury stock buybacks by listed companies for three months, from November 24, 2026 through February 23, 2027, as part of the government's emergency market stabilization package.

rok_government.action: COP31 closes in Turkey without cover decision; Korea calls it first major climate agreement collapse since 2009 Copenhagen
rok_government.detail: The 31st UN Framework Convention on Climate Change Conference of Parties (COP31) closed in Antalya, Turkey on November 23, two days late and without adopting a cover decision, which MOFA described as the first failure to reach a comprehensive climate agreement since the 2009 Copenhagen summit. South Korea's delegation was led by Climate-Energy-Environment Minister Kim Sung-hwan.

rok_assembly.action: Defense Minister Kang Shin-cheol answers committee questions
rok_assembly.detail: Defense Minister Kang Shin-cheol appeared before the National Assembly defense committee for a plenary session, responding to questions from lawmakers.

overnight_items.headline: North Korean vessel marked 'Marine Police' spotted near Yeonpyeong Island; ROK Joint Chiefs tracking
overnight_items.body_text: ROK Joint Chiefs confirmed they are tracking and monitoring the vessel.

overnight_items.headline: South Korea education minister Choi Kyo-jin, 72, resigns saying he is too old to handle AI cheating
overnight_items.body_text: Said he was too old to tackle AI-enabled exam abuses.

overnight_items.headline: South Korea seeks IAEA safeguards for nuclear-powered submarines
overnight_items.body_text: Seoul formally pursuing IAEA verification for its nuclear submarine program.

overnight_items.headline: Saudi Arabia turns to South Korea and others to procure air-defense systems against attacks
overnight_items.body_text: Seoul among suppliers Riyadh is approaching for counter-attack defense systems.

overnight_items.headline: Low-income Sinuiju families sinking into crisis as state touts border city as development model
overnight_items.body_text: Food and daily necessity prices soaring despite state 'heaven-and-earth transformation' narrative.

overnight_items.headline: Team Korea vows to complete Czech Dukovany nuclear plant on schedule despite contractor dispute
overnight_items.body_text: Korean consortium committed to on-time delivery despite construction contractor dispute.

overnight_items.headline: Luxury for DPRK elite, hardship for masses: North Korea's economic divide
overnight_items.body_text: Analysis documents Kim Ju-ae's ski gear sparking sanctions questions alongside mass poverty.

overnight_items.headline: Analysis: Why Kim Jong Un keeps snubbing Trump's dialogue offers
overnight_items.body_text: Kim inspected educational factory sites the same week Trump's outreach went unanswered.

capitol_hill.headline: Sen. Coons warns North Korea growing more lethal through Ukraine cooperation
capitol_hill.body_text: Democratic Sen. Chris Coons of Delaware, speaking at the Halifax International Security Forum, warned that North Korea's troop and equipment cooperation with Russia, China, and Iran now constrains Washington's freedom to act and is producing a more capable North Korean military.

capitol_hill.headline: Korea-US alliance friction: Seoul told to urgently build new US Congress relations
capitol_hill.body_text: An analysis outlet reported calls for the South Korean government to urgently build working relationships with the new US Congress amid turbulence in the Korea-US bilateral relationship, with midterm election results producing new defenders of the alliance on Capitol Hill.

korea_world.headline: Korean-French-Vietnamese consortium wins $397M consultancy for Vietnam North-South high-speed railway
korea_world.body_text: A consortium of eight Vietnamese, French, and South Korean companies, including Korea National Railway Corp., Sambo Engineering, and Yooshin Engineering, was selected for a *$397 million* consultancy package for Vietnam's North-South high-speed railway, the largest contract awarded for the project.

korea_world.headline: Seoul says Cheonghae anti-piracy unit expansion near Oman is not participation in Iran war
korea_world.body_text: South Korea's government stated its planned expansion of the Cheonghae anti-piracy mission near Oman does not constitute indirect military participation in the US-Iran conflict, amid domestic political pressure and legal scrutiny over the deployment's scope.

korea_world.headline: Seoul asks Qatar to prioritize LNG supplies to South Korea once Hormuz shipping normalizes
korea_world.body_text: South Korea asked Qatar to give Seoul priority status for liquefied natural gas supplies once production and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz return to normal following the US-Iran conflict.

kcna_delta.kim_activity: Kim Jong Un personally received credentials from 10 newly appointed ambassadors at the Workers' Party of Korea Central Committee headquarters on November 22, delivering a speech on DPRK foreign policy and arms buildup.

top_articles.headline: North Korean party cell leaders to attend conference
top_articles.summary: KCNA announced that North Korean Workers' Party cell leaders will convene for a conference.

key_quotes.speaker: Kim Jong Un
key_quotes.quote: The security situation in the DPRK and the political and military environment in East Asia urgently demand that we provide for ourselves the power and capability.
key_quotes.context: Ambassador credentials ceremony, Nov 22, on DPRK military buildup as self-defense
key_quotes.source_article: N. Korea's Kim says Pyongyang seeks no regional dominance, defending arms buildup as self-defense

senior_officials.name: Choe Son Hui
senior_officials.activity: Choe Son Hui attended the ambassador credentials ceremony at the Workers' Party of Korea Central Committee headquarters on November 22.

kcna_delta.bottom_line: State media led with Kim's first-ever direct reception of foreign ambassadors' credentials and his assertion that North Korea's military buildup constitutes self-defense, with domestic content covering a party cell leaders' conference; the failed Trump summit offer remained absent from KCNA output.

calendar_watch.headline: Unification Ministry AI deliberation platform conference, Seoul National University
calendar_watch.detail: The Ministry of Unification and Seoul National University co-host an international academic conference on the Korean-model AI deliberation platform 'Hongik' and civil dialogue on peace and unification, featuring speakers including Taiwan's former cyber ambassador Audrey Tang.

calendar_watch.headline: FSC treasury stock buyback rule ease takes effect
calendar_watch.detail: The Financial Services Commission's three-month easing of the daily buying-order limit on treasury stock buybacks by listed companies takes effect, running through February 23, 2027.

calendar_watch.headline: Korea-China high-speed rail seminar, Seoul Press Center
calendar_watch.detail: The Ministry of Unification and Korea Railroad Research Institute co-host an international seminar on the Korea-China high-speed railway concept, featuring Korean and Chinese rail and trade experts discussing Northeast Asia rail network connectivity.
